item.title: Building a homebrew monitoring dashboard with Grafana + iSpindel
item.description: I wanted a better way to track how my homebrews were going. In any brew, the most important metric to keep an eye on is the specific gravity - a measure of density. This will tell you where in the fermentation you’re at, how much further it has to go, and what the ABV% is. Checking this value periodically, will let you work out how quickly your brew is fermenting, and when might be a good time to add extra hops, and when it’s ready to bottle.

item.title: Hacking a standing desk to raise for meetings
item.description: Inspired by this post and noticing that my standing desk seemed to have the same control panel, I wanted to do something similar. One thing I wanted to change though is when the desk should be triggered to raise. In that post the author added a random interval of 45 to 60 minutes. Instead I wanted to stand only for my meetings. I’ve found that I can’t stand when I’m actually trying to get focused work done, and having my desk randomly raise and break my concentration when I didn’t expect it to did not sound appealing.

item.title: Syncing local python packages to Google Colab
item.description: This post goes through how to set up a one-way sync of a local python package to a Google Colab instance using cloudflared, lsyncd and some jupyter magic. This allows you to work on a package locally in your IDE of choice and have it automatically stay in sync with the version imported into your notebook. Within a couple of seconds of making a change locally, your changes are auto-reloaded into your running notebook without having to re-import anything. This example is focusing on using a python package but that’s not a requirement. Ultimately we’re just syncing a local directory to a remote one so this could be used in various ways, eg. syncing config files that you want your notebook code to pick up.
